name: People’s Republic of China
summary: Proclaimed in 1949 after the civil war. After decades of upheaval, reforms from 1978 transformed it into the world’s second-largest economy.

knownFor.label: High-speed rail
knownFor.note: The world’s largest high-speed rail network.

location.value: East Asia, with Beijing as capital. Area about 9.6 million km².

terrain.value: The Tibetan plateau, deserts in the northwest, the Yellow and Yangtze river plains, and a long Pacific coast.
terrain.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

climate.value: Varied, from subarctic to tropical. It faces air pollution and water stress.
climate.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

resources.value: Coal, rare earths, farmland and a huge labour force.
resources.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

disasters.value: The Great Chinese Famine (1959–61) during the Great Leap Forward, with an estimated 15–55 million deaths. The Tangshan earthquake (1976). The 2008 Sichuan earthquake.

urbanisation.value: Over 68% urban in 2025, after one of history’s largest migrations from countryside to city.

disease.value: COVID-19 was first identified in Wuhan in late 2019.

migration.value: The one-child policy (1979–2015) shaped population, and limits were removed in 2021. Hundreds of millions of rural migrants moved to cities.

economicBase.value: A state-led market economy since the 1978 reforms. It produced about 28% of global manufacturing (2024).

tradeRoutes.value: The world’s largest exporter. It joined the WTO (2001) and launched the Belt and Road Initiative (2013).
tradeRoutes.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

wealth.value: The world’s second-largest economy by GDP and the largest by purchasing power. Average growth was over 9% a year after 1978, and about 800 million people were lifted out of extreme poverty.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: China (checked 6 Nov 2026); World Bank: China overview

inequality.value: Gini about 36 (2022). Large gaps between coast and interior, and between urban and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A one-party socialist state led by the Chinese Communist Party, proclaimed on 1 October 1949.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

keyRulers.value: Mao Zedong (1949–1976). Deng Xiaoping (from 1978). Jiang Zemin (1989–2002). Hu Jintao (2002–2012). Xi Jinping (from 2012).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Decided within the Communist Party leadership. Presidential term limits were removed in 2018.
succession.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

institutions.value: The Communist Party, the National People’s Congress, and the People’s Liberation Army (about 2 million active soldiers).

stability.value: Political campaigns (the Anti-Rightist Campaign, the Cultural Revolution 1966–76), and the Tiananmen Square protests, ended by force on 3–4 June 1989.
stability.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

eliteConflict.value: Power struggles at the top (e.g. the Gang of Four, arrested 1976), and anti-corruption purges since 2012.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

armyAndTech.value: The PLA, the world’s largest standing army. Nuclear weapons since 1964. A rapidly modernising navy.
armyAndTech.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

majorWars.value: The Korean War (1950–53). The Sino-Indian War (1962). The Sino-Vietnamese War (1979).
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: Took control of Tibet (1950–51). Hong Kong (1997) and Macau (1999) were handed over by Britain and Portugal. Claims Taiwan, which is governed by the ROC. Disputes in the South China Sea.

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with the USSR (1950s), then the Sino-Soviet split. Rapprochement with the US (Nixon, 1972). Now strategic rivalry with the US.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

inventions.value: First satellite (1970), first astronauts (2003), the Tiangong space station (crewed since 2021), high-speed rail, and telecommunications.

scienceEducation.value: Mass literacy campaigns, and a rapidly expanding university and research system. Universities were disrupted during the Cultural Revolution.
scienceEducation.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

openness.value: Closed under Mao. “Reform and opening up” from 1978. Tight control of the internet and the media.
openness.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

communicationTransport.value: The world’s largest high-speed rail network (from 2008), expressways and mobile payment apps.

religion.value: Officially atheist. Buddhism, Taoism, folk religion, Islam and Christianity exist under state regulation.
religion.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

languageWriting.value: Standard Chinese (Mandarin) in simplified characters (from the 1950s), plus many regional and minority languages.

artsArchitecture.value: Revolutionary art (Mao era), then modern film, literature (Mo Yan, Nobel Prize 2012) and architecture.
artsArchitecture.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

socialStructure.value: Han Chinese are about 91% of the population. The hukou registration system divides urban and rural citizens.

sharedIdentity.value: Chinese nationalism, socialism “with Chinese characteristics”, and the goal of national rejuvenation.
sharedIdentity.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

dailyLife.value: From rural houses to high-rise apartments; rice, noodles, dumplings; huge migration to cities.

neighbours.value: 14 land neighbours, including Russia, India, Vietnam, North Korea, Mongolia, Pakistan and Central Asian states.

ideasReligions.value: Exported Maoism in the Cold War, and now development finance and trade (Belt and Road).
ideasReligions.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

colonisation.value: Not a colonial power in the classic sense. According to Wikipedia, China has persecuted the Uyghur population in Xinjiang, interning over a million people in camps, and cracked down on political expression in Tibet. The Chinese government rejects these characterisations.

riseSignals.value: Victory in the civil war (1949), then the 1978 market reforms, opening to trade, and massive investment.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: History of the People's Republic of China (checked 6 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: Ongoing: rose to become the world’s second-largest economy.

declineSignals.value: Not in decline. Debated challenges include an ageing population, debt, slowing growth and tensions with the US.
declineSignals.source: Fenby, The Penguin History of Modern China (2019)

outcome.value: Ongoing: a one-party socialist state and a major world power.

sources.value: Official statistics (sometimes questioned), the 2020 census, and modern histories. Checked against Wikipedia (“China”, “History of the PRC”) on 6 Nov 2026 (some infobox figures came from summaries). See also Fenby (2019).

overallCertainty.value: Good for events. Famine and Cultural Revolution death tolls, Tibet, Xinjiang and Taiwan are highly contested, so this entry quotes neutral wording from the sources.
